subject: [PATCH v1 0/3] mm/readahead: avoid per-folio memcg reclaim

reviews.author: Jan Kara
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Jan Kara noted that the patch does not handle the case where a folio is already locked by another thread when try_to_unmap() is called, and requested that the lock be dropped before calling try_to_unmap().

The reviewer agrees that the current read-ahead logic for mmap is flawed, as confirmed by Joanne's tracing results.

Reviewer Jan Kara noted that the detection of whether fault-around pages are being used has been broken since the addition of filemap_map_pages(), which also broke mmap_miss accounting, and requested a fix to this issue before implementing logic to size readaround sensibly.

Jan Kara suggested using an xarray tag to track readahead information, referencing the additional xarray tags available in the maple tree

The reviewer noted that the patch is mostly independent from the issue being addressed and did not provide any specific technical feedback or suggestions.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Joanne!

On Tue 06-10-26 16:01:28, Joanne Koong wrote:

---

Thanks for looking into this quickly! So basically your tracing seems to
confirm my suspicion our read-around logic for mmap is quite bad.

---

So I think we definitely need to fix the detection whether the fault-around
pages are getting used or not because since we've added filemap_map_pages()
the mmap_miss accounting was broken. And once that signal is fixed, we can
come up with some logic to size the readaround sensibly.

---

Yes, something like that would be a good indication our readahead isn't
working as it should. But the problem he is how to track this information
with the folio... Maybe as an xarray tag? Liam was mentioning to me a few
days ago that with maple tree we have more xarray tags available ;).

---

Yes, they are related but mostly independent from the issue you're
addressing in this series.

								Honza
-- 
Jan Kara <jack@suse.com>
SUSE Labs, CR

2026-10-07.patch_summary: This patch series addresses a performance issue in Linux's readahead mechanism by avoiding per-folio memory cgroup (memcg) reclaim. When multiple tasks fault in the same cgroup, the frequent per-folio charges trigger reclaim, leading to livelocks and high CPU usage. The patches modify readahead to charge all folios in its window at once when the memcg is at its limit, reducing the number of reclaim passes by 94-96% and eliminating livelocks on a test system with btrfs file systems and compress-force=zstd:3.
